packet.answer:
Bringing a lamp to the repair café? Please use the side door and arrive by 6 p.m. Friday.

I changed “the usual entrance” to “the side door” because a first-time visitor wouldn’t know which entrance we usually use.
packet.evidence_limit: Review covers the submitted passage and its editing rationale. Several voices and arrangements can serve the same reader. Whether real readers understood it needs a reader observation. Fiction, poetry, the learner's overall talent and any private writing remain outside this finding.
packet.goal: I want to learn how to be a better writer

material.practice: The draft for a free reading says, 'Use it to save your place.' The brief says seats can be reserved by emailing the library desk. Write a line for someone attending for the first time. Which part of the original would have made them stop?
material.worked: A film-club draft says, 'Pick up one at the table.' The brief says that first-time guests collect a program at the table beside the lift. One revision is 'Want a program? Pick one up beside the lift.' Naming the program and landmark helps a guest who has never seen that table. A quieter sentence could do the same job.

packet.policy: Ask for a draft passage and what the writer wants the passage to do for its reader. Use the passage and the stated purpose to select one writing move. Show it in a short worked example, then ask the writer to try it on the passage and explain their choice. At the end, propose one short goal for future writing based on the purpose the writer explicitly stated. Record the exact wording only after the writer approves it. If the writer declines or gives no approval, save nothing from this exchange.
packet.task: A repair café needs a notice for a first-time visitor bringing a lamp. Visitors bringing a lamp use the side door by 6 p.m. Friday. Volunteers use the main entrance. The draft reads, 'Please come to the usual entrance by the deadline.' Write your version for that visitor, then explain one edit in terms of what the reader needs. Choose your own voice.

response.display:
You changed “the usual entrance” to “the side door” because a first-time visitor needs a door they can identify. The film-club example uses the same move: “beside the lift” gives new guests a landmark. Try applying that move to timing in your notice. Rewrite “by 6 p.m. Friday” in your own voice, or keep it as written, and explain how your choice helps a first-time visitor plan their arrival.

For your goal of becoming a better writer, would you approve this wording? “Give first-time readers the details they need to act.”
